# vastdata_de_pipeline (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
# Create a Data Engine pipeline linking a schedule trigger to a function,
# then deploy it (default) and wait until status is Ready.
# Exactly one of kubernetes_cluster_vrn or kubernetes_cluster_name.

resource "vastdata_de_pipeline" "hello" {
  name                    = "de-test-pipeline"
  tenant_name             = "de-lab"
  kubernetes_cluster_name = vastdata_de_kubernetes_cluster.example.name
  namespace               = "vast-pipelines"
  deploy                  = true

  manifest = {
    triggers = [
      {
        name = vastdata_de_schedule_trigger.hello.name
        vrn  = vastdata_de_schedule_trigger.hello.vrn
      }
    ]
    function_deployments = [
      {
        name         = "hello-fn"
        function_vrn = vastdata_de_function.hello.vrn
      }
    ]
    links = [
      {
        source      = [vastdata_de_schedule_trigger.hello.name]
        destination = ["hello-fn"]
      }
    ]
  }
}

# ---------------------
# Complete examples
# ---------------------

# Undeployed pipeline with per-function config, secrets, configmaps,
# event batching, and resource limits.
resource "vastdata_de_pipeline" "advanced_undeployed" {
  name                   = "de-pipe-advanced"
  tenant_name            = "de-lab"
  kubernetes_cluster_vrn = vastdata_de_kubernetes_cluster.example.vrn
  namespace              = "vast-pipelines"
  deploy                 = false
  description            = "Undeployed pipeline with advanced function deployment options"
  tags                   = ["example", "advanced"]

  depends_on = [vastdata_de_kubernetes_secret.example]

  manifest = {
    triggers = [
      {
        name = vastdata_de_schedule_trigger.hello.name
        vrn  = vastdata_de_schedule_trigger.hello.vrn
      },
    ]
    function_deployments = [
      {
        name         = "hello-fn"
        function_vrn = vastdata_de_function.hello.vrn
        config = {
          log_level = "DEBUG"
          secrets   = [vastdata_de_kubernetes_secret.example.secret_name]
          environment_variables = [
            { name = "PIPE_KIND", value = "advanced" },
          ]
          configmaps = [
            {
              name = "de-pipe-cm"
              data = { kind = "advanced" }
            },
          ]
          event_batching = {
            batch_max_size   = 5
            batch_timeout_ms = 1000
          }
        }
        resources = {
          min_cpu         = "100m"
          max_cpu         = "500m"
          min_memory      = "128Mi"
          max_memory      = "256Mi"
          timeout         = 60
          num_workers     = 4
          max_concurrency = 10
        }
      },
    ]
    links = [
      {
        source      = [vastdata_de_schedule_trigger.hello.name]
        destination = ["hello-fn"]
      },
    ]
    config = {
      secrets = [vastdata_de_kubernetes_secret.example.secret_name]
      environment_variables = [
        { name = "PIPE_SCOPE", value = "pipeline" },
      ]
    }
  }
}

# --------------------

# Element-trigger-only graph (no schedule).
resource "vastdata_de_pipeline" "element_only" {
  name                   = "de-pipe-element"
  tenant_name            = "de-lab"
  kubernetes_cluster_vrn = vastdata_de_kubernetes_cluster.example.vrn
  namespace              = "vast-pipelines"
  deploy                 = false
  description            = "Pipeline driven only by an element (S3) trigger"
  tags                   = ["example", "element"]

  manifest = {
    triggers = [
      {
        name = vastdata_de_element_trigger.example.name
        vrn  = vastdata_de_element_trigger.example.vrn
      },
    ]
    function_deployments = [
      {
        name         = "hello-fn"
        function_vrn = vastdata_de_function.hello.vrn
      },
    ]
    links = [
      {
        source      = [vastdata_de_element_trigger.example.name]
        destination = ["hello-fn"]
      },
    ]
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `manifest` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--manifest))
- `name` (String) A name for the resource.
- `namespace` (String) The namespace in the kubernetes cluster

### Optional

- `deploy` (Boolean) When true (default), POST /pipeline/{guid}/deploy after create/update and wait until status is Ready.
- `description` (String) A description of the resource.
- `kubernetes_cluster_name` (String) Kubernetes cluster name. Resolved to a VRN before create/update. Exactly one of kubernetes_cluster_vrn or kubernetes_cluster_name must be set.
- `kubernetes_cluster_vrn` (String) Kubernetes cluster VRN (vast:dataengine:kubernetes-clusters:...). Exactly one of kubernetes_cluster_vrn or kubernetes_cluster_name must be set.
- `tags` (List of String) Custom tags for organizing and categorizing resources in the GUI.
- `tenant_name` (String) Tenant name for Data Engine API queries. Required for cluster-admin auth; optional when the provider already authenticates as that tenant.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the resource was created.
- `guid` (String) A globally unique identifier (GUID) for the resource.
- `id` (Number) A globally unique identifier (ID) for the resource.
- `last_revision_number` (Number) The latest revision number
- `owner` (Attributes) Represents the owner of the resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--owner))
- `reason` (String) The reason for status current
- `stack_guid` (String) A globally unique identifier (GUID) for the resource.
- `stack_revision_number` (Number) Revision number of the stack that created this pipeline (null if created directly)
- `status` (String) The status of pipeline deployment
- `tenant_guid` (String) A globally unique identifier (GUID) for the resource.
- `updated_at` (String) Timestamp when the resource was last updated.
- `used_resources` (Map of Set of Object) Per-function-deployment resource usage, keyed by function deployment name. Each value is the list of pod resources for that function deployment (empty when scaled to zero).
- `vrn` (String) A logical path for resource grouping and policy assignment. The structure of the logical path is: vast:dataengine:<resource type>:<custom structure per type>
where resource type is one of: triggers / functions / pipelines / topics / kubernetes-clusters / container-registries / mtls-authentication-credentials.

<a id="nestedatt--manifest--function_deployments--resources"></a>
### Nested Schema for `manifest.function_deployments.resources`

Optional:

- `autoscaling` (Attributes) Autoscaling configuration for the function deployment. Defines how the function
scales based on incoming requests or resource utilization.

Three autoscaling metrics are supported:
- concurrency: Scale based on concurrent requests per instance (default, supports scale-to-zero)
- rps: Scale based on requests per second per instance (supports scale-to-zero)
- resource: Scale based on CPU or memory utilization (does not support scale-to-zero)

Only one of 'concurrency', 'rps', or 'resource' should be provided, matching the 'metric' field. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--manifest--function_deployments--resources--autoscaling))
- `autoscaling_concurrency_overload_factor` (String) Deprecated: Use 'autoscaling' field instead with type='kpa_concurrency'.

Autoscaling concurrency overload factor (> 0.0). Determines when to scale based on 
concurrency overload beyond current processing capacity. When concurrency exceeds 
(capacity * (1 + overload_factor)), new function instances are created.

For backward compatibility, if this field is set and 'autoscaling' is not provided,
concurrency metric autoscaling will be used with target_utilization_percentage calculated
from this value.

Default: "0.05" (5% overload tolerance)
- `autoscaling_rps_factor` (Number) Deprecated: This field is no longer used and will be removed in a future version. It is ignored if provided.
- `max_concurrency` (Number) 10
- `max_concurrent_requests_limit` (Number) Maximum number of concurrent requests the function can handle per instance.
This represents how many requests can be processed simultaneously (in-flight)
by a single function instance. Maps to Knative `spec.containerConcurrency`.

If omitted, the value is computed at deploy time as
`max(num_workers, batch_max_size)` (defaults: `max(20, 1) = 20`).
This ensures the queue-proxy enforces backpressure per pod so the
autoscaler can scale out instead of all traffic piling on a single pod.

Set explicitly to `0` for unlimited per-pod concurrency (queue-proxy
does not throttle). Use with caution: with `0` the autoscaler cannot
observe queue pressure and may keep traffic on a single instance.

Setting this value below the actual function capacity will hurt performance.
Set ONLY if you know an upper bound for the capacity; this applies
backpressure on a loaded function instance and waits for autoscale
instead of queueing requests, which can tune performance and avoid
timed-out requests in the queue and retries.

WARNING: If autoscaling is configured with concurrency metric (or the deprecated autoscaling_concurrency_overload_factor),
this value must be GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO the target value. Otherwise the effective target for autoscaling will be the MINIMUM of this value and the target value.
- `max_cpu` (String)
- `max_memory` (String)
- `min_concurrency` (Number)
- `min_cpu` (String)
- `min_memory` (String)
- `num_workers` (Number) Number of worker threads per function instance.             
When event batching is enabled, the effective concurrency per instance is 
num_workers * batch_max_size, since each worker processes one batch at a time.
Default: 20 (matches the default Python runtime worker threads)
Maximum: 100
- `storage` (String)
- `timeout` (Number) Timeout in seconds for the function deployment.

<a id="nestedatt--manifest--function_deployments--resources--autoscaling"></a>
### Nested Schema for `manifest.function_deployments.resources.autoscaling`

Required:

- `metric` (String) The metric used for autoscaling decisions. Determines which configuration object should be provided:
- concurrency: Provide 'concurrency' configuration object
- rps: Provide 'rps' configuration object
- resource: Provide 'resource' configuration object

Optional:

- `concurrency` (Attributes) Autoscaling configuration based on concurrent requests metric.
Extends RequestAutoscalingConfig with concurrency-specific options. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--manifest--function_deployments--resources--autoscaling--concurrency))
- `resource` (Attributes) Autoscaling configuration based on resource utilization (CPU or memory).

Note: Resource-based autoscaling does not support scale-to-zero. 
Use concurrency or rps metrics if scale-to-zero is required. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--manifest--function_deployments--resources--autoscaling--resource))
- `rps` (Attributes) Common autoscaling configuration for request-based metrics (concurrency and RPS).
This configuration supports scale-to-zero when there is no traffic. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--manifest--function_deployments--resources--autoscaling--rps))

<a id="nestedatt--manifest--function_deployments--resources--autoscaling--concurrency"></a>
### Nested Schema for `manifest.function_deployments.resources.autoscaling.concurrency`

Optional:

- `burst_threshold_percentage` (Number) Burst mode threshold as a percentage of current capacity (110-1000).
Burst mode is triggered when traffic exceeds this percentage of what
current instances can handle.

For example, 200 means burst mode starts when traffic is 2x current capacity.
- `burst_window_percentage` (Number) Burst detection window as a percentage of stable window (1-100).
Defines the shorter time window used to detect traffic bursts.
Lower values make burst detection more sensitive.
- `hard_limit` (Number) Hard limit for concurrent requests per instance. Surplus requests will be buffered
until capacity is available. Set to 0 for unlimited (default).

Warning: Using a hard limit may negatively impact throughput and latency.
Only recommended if there's a clear use case for limiting concurrency.
- `scale_down_delay_seconds` (Number) Delay in seconds before scaling down after load decreases.
Helps prevent thrashing during fluctuating traffic.
- `scale_to_zero_delay_seconds` (Number) Minimum time in seconds to retain the last instance before scaling to zero.
The instance is kept for at least this duration after the autoscaler decides to scale to zero.
- `stable_window_seconds` (Number) Time window in seconds for stable autoscaling decisions (6 to 3600).
Larger values result in more smoothing.

When scaling to zero, the last instance is only removed after no traffic
for the entire duration of this window.
- `target` (Number) Target value per instance. The autoscaler will try to maintain this level per instance.
- For concurrency metric: target number of concurrent requests (default: 20, which matches
  the default number of worker threads in non-asyncio Python functions)
- For RPS metric: target requests per second
- `target_utilization_percentage` (Number) Target utilization percentage (1-100). Specifies what percentage of the target
should actually be targeted by the autoscaler. This causes the autoscaler to
scale up before the target is reached.

For example, with target=10 and target_utilization_percentage=70, the autoscaler
will create a new instance when average metric value reaches 7.


<a id="nestedatt--manifest--function_deployments--resources--autoscaling--resource"></a>
### Nested Schema for `manifest.function_deployments.resources.autoscaling.resource`

Required:

- `resource_autoscaling_type` (String) The resource type to use for autoscaling:
- cpu: Scale based on CPU utilization percentage
- memory: Scale based on memory utilization percentage
- `target` (Number) Target value for the selected resource.
For CPU, this is the target utilization percentage (e.g., 80 means 80% of CPU request).
Note: The Knative documentation at https://knative.dev/docs/serving/autoscaling/autoscaling-metrics/
incorrectly states this is in millicores, but testing and Knative source code confirm it's a percentage.
For memory, this is in Mi (e.g., 200 means 200Mi).
The HPA will scale when actual usage exceeds this target.

Optional:

- `stable_window_seconds` (Number) Time window in seconds for stable autoscaling decisions (6 to 3600).
This controls the HPA stabilization window for scale-down decisions.
Larger values result in more smoothing and slower scale-down.
Default: not set (uses Kubernetes HPA default of 300s)

- `stable_window_seconds` (Number) Time window in seconds for stable autoscaling decisions (6 to 3600).
Larger values result in more smoothing.

When scaling to zero, the last instance is only removed after no traffic

- `target` (Number) Target value per instance. The autoscaler will try to maintain this level per instance.
- For concurrency metric: target number of concurrent requests (default: 20, which matches

- For RPS metric: target requests per second
- `target_utilization_percentage` (Number) Target utilization percentage (1-100). Specifies what percentage of the target

For example, with target=10 and target_utilization_percentage=70, the autoscaler
